speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned presenting with gait and limb ataxia; can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they are progressive? Also, what significant medical conditions or prior treatments do you have in your history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis. While the symptoms of gait and limb ataxia are consistent with cerebellar involvement seen in MS, the "recent" onset described by the patient contradicts the typical progressive nature of ataxia in established MS or suggests an acute demyelinating event like a brainstem stroke. Given the significant medical history you mentioned but did not specify, and the unilateral predominance on the right side, an acute ischemic stroke or a tumor must be ruled out immediately. I will request a Brain MRI to visualize the posterior fossa and cerebellum. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI
